title: "Tell me about yourself"
examples: How long should my self-introduction be for a networking event?
What is the best way to transition from my past experience to my future goals?
Should I include my hobbies in a professional self-introduction?

explain.say: We will start by looking at how to talk about your past experience.

items: Use specific achievements, not just duties.

draw.text: Past Experience: What have you done?

explain.say: Next, we need to connect that past to your present skills and focus.

draw.text: Present Focus: What are you good at now?

explain.say: Then, we must look ahead to your future goals and aspirations.

draw.text: Future Goals: Where are you going next?

explain.say: Putting it all together, we will structure this into a concise sixty-second pitch.
In a real job interview, you can use this structure to guide your answer.

items: Row 3: Future | Show alignment with the job

explain.say: A common mistake is listing every job you have ever held.

items: Only select roles relevant to the job.
Focus on impact, not just duration.
Keep the narrative focused and brief.

faq.q: How do I make sure my pitch sounds natural and not memorized?
faq.a: Practice the key points out loud many times. Focus on the flow between sections rather than memorizing every word. You can also use bullet points as prompts during practice.
asks: Should I write out a script for practice?

faq.q: If I am changing careers, how do I bridge the gap between my old field and the new one?
faq.a: Identify transferable skills. For example, if you managed projects before, you can say you bring strong organizational skills to this new field. Connect the skill directly to the new job's needs.
asks: What if my experience is totally different?
How do I explain a career pivot?

faq.q: Should I tailor my pitch for every single job I apply for?
faq.a: Yes, absolutely. Your pitch must speak directly to the requirements listed in the job description. Think of it as customizing your sales pitch for one specific client.
asks: Is one pitch good enough for many jobs?
How specific do I need to be?

faq.q: What is the best way to handle questions about salary expectations during this introduction?
faq.a: It is often best to wait until later in the interview process to discuss specific numbers. You can instead express your enthusiasm for the role's potential impact.
asks: When should I talk about money?
Can I avoid salary talk early on?

faq.q: If I have gaps in my employment history, should I mention them?
faq.a: Do not bring up the gap unless you are asked directly. If you must address it, frame it positively, perhaps mentioning professional development or personal study during that time.
asks: What if I took time off for family?
How do I explain unemployment gaps?

facts: A standard 'elevator pitch' should be concise, usually under one minute.
The structure generally moves from past accomplishments to current skills, then to future goals.
Transferable skills are abilities gained in one area that apply to another field.
Tailoring your pitch shows the interviewer that you have done your research.

quiz.say: When structuring your pitch, what should be the primary focus of the 'Present' section?

options.show: Listing every job title you have held.
options.say: Listing every job title you have held.

options.say: Talking only about your future dreams.

quiz.why: This section proves you are immediately valuable to the role.

wrong.1: This wastes time and dilutes your main message.
wrong.2: While important, it misses your practical, applicable skills.
wrong.3: You must first prove your capability with past and present work.

options.show: Only mentioning skills learned in school.
options.say: Only mentioning skills learned in school.

quiz.why: This shows employers that your core abilities are adaptable.

wrong.0: This overlooks valuable professional experience you already have.
wrong.2: This makes you seem unprepared or lacking depth.
wrong.3: Never sound apologetic; sound determined and strategic instead.

quiz.say: A pitch that is too long often fails because:

options.show: The speaker forgets the main points.
options.say: The speaker forgets the main points.

quiz.why: Conciseness keeps the listener engaged and respectful of their time.

wrong.0: This is too subjective; the issue is structural pacing.
wrong.1: The goal is professional connection, not academic review.
wrong.3: While possible, the primary issue is audience attention span.
